docs.summary:
Bakes and registers a navmesh for one agent type. The baked result is a standalone [`NavMeshData`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshData) asset, which the surface registers with the scene's [`NavMeshWorld`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshWorld) on enable. Rebuilds run synchronously, in the background ([`BuildNavMeshAsync`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshSurface~BuildNavMeshAsync)), or per-tile for localized geometry changes ([`RebuildTiles`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshSurface~RebuildTiles)).

Registration is the whole of this component's lifecycle — there is no per-frame work — and it runs in the editor as well as in play: obstacles can only carve a live navmesh and the overlay draws one, so without it a scene's baked navmesh stays unregistered until something bakes again.

The resolved bake input: the agent type's envelope composed with this surface's [`BuildOverrides`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshSurface~BuildOverrides). What gets handed to [`Build`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshBuilder~Build); a fresh snapshot each call.
The live navmesh registration, while enabled and a navmesh is loaded.

What the live navmesh was built from, and what rebuilds rewrite. Null while unregistered. For a `.navmesh` asset this is a private copy made at registration, because the object the database hands out is shared by every surface pointing at it and by the next scene that loads it. For a navmesh built at runtime and handed over through [`ApplyNavMeshData`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshSurface~ApplyNavMeshData) it is that object itself — nothing else owns it.
Called when the object becomes enabled and active. Only called when the GameObject is in a Scene and enabled.
Called when the object becomes disabled or inactive. Only called when the GameObject was in a Scene and becomes disabled.

Collect geometry and bake the navmesh synchronously, then (re)register it with the scene. Blocks the calling thread for the duration of the bake — prefer [`BuildNavMeshAsync`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshSurface~BuildNavMeshAsync) during gameplay.

Collect geometry and bake synchronously, returning the result without registering it. For callers that persist the bake first and register the saved asset instead, so the tiles are meshed once rather than once per registration.

Bake in the background: geometry is collected on the calling (main) thread, the voxelization runs on the thread pool. Apply the result with [`ApplyNavMeshData`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshSurface~ApplyNavMeshData) from the main thread when the task completes.
Swap in a freshly built navmesh: replaces this surface's data (as a runtime resource) and its registration in the scene. Main thread only.
Re-register the currently assigned [`NavMeshData`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshData) (e.g. after the asset reference was swapped by an editor bake).

Rebuild only the tiles intersecting `worldBounds` against the current scene geometry (via this surface's collectors) and swap them into the live navmesh — cost scales with the changed volume, not the map size. The tile grid stays anchored to the original bake, so geometry outside the original bounds needs a full [`BuildNavMesh`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshSurface~BuildNavMesh). Requires an enabled surface with a registered navmesh.

members.name: RebuildLinkTiles
members.signature: public bool RebuildLinkTiles(ReadOnlySpan<AABB> worldBounds, IReadOnlyList<NavMeshLinkSource>? links = null)

docs.summary: Replace the live link set and re-contour the tiles overlapping `worldBounds`. No re-voxelization: the compressed layers are untouched, which is what makes this cheap next to [`RebuildTiles`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshSurface~RebuildTiles). False when this surface has no live navmesh.

params.worldBounds: Regions whose tiles pick up the change, normally around link endpoints. A tile several of them cover re-contours once, which is the point of handing a frame's link edits over together.
params.links: The surface's complete link set. Null collects the scene's [`NavMeshLink`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshLink)s.

docs.summary:
World rect the collectors must cover for a rebuild of `worldBounds`: the affected TILES plus the erosion border, because rebuilds rasterize whole tiles. Null when there is no grid to derive it from, meaning collect everything.

Public because the explicit-sources overload makes covering this rect the caller's job, and getting it wrong leaves holes rather than failing. Collectors clip terrain to the filter they are given, so the changed AABB alone is not conservative.

members.name: RebuildTiles
members.signature: public bool RebuildTiles(AABB worldBounds, IReadOnlyList<NavMeshGeometrySource> sources, IReadOnlyList<NavMeshAreaVolume>? volumes = null)

docs.summary: Rebuild the tiles intersecting `worldBounds` from caller-supplied geometry, for games whose world the collectors cannot see. Pass the bounds of the CHANGED geometry; the affected tile set derives from them plus the erosion border, and [`RebuildCollectionBounds`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshSurface~RebuildCollectionBounds) returns exactly the rect to collect against. Covering less is not a cheaper rebuild — partly covered tiles come back with holes. An empty source list is valid and empties the affected tiles.

params.sources: The geometry to bake the affected tiles from.
params.volumes: Area volumes applied to the rebuilt tiles. Null (the default) collects the scene's [`NavMeshModifierVolume`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshModifierVolume)s over the affected region — note that collection walks the scene's active objects, so callers who chose explicit sources to avoid scene scans should pass an empty list (no volumes, no scan) or their own list.

members.name: RebuildTilesAsync
members.signature: public Task<List<NavMeshTileRebuild>> RebuildTilesAsync(AABB worldBounds, IReadOnlyList<NavMeshGeometrySource> sources, CancellationToken cancellation = default, IReadOnlyList<NavMeshAreaVolume>? volumes = null)

docs.summary: Voxelize the affected tiles on the thread pool, off the frame. The returned tiles are NOT yet live — apply them with [`ApplyRebuiltTiles`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshSurface~ApplyRebuiltTiles) from the main thread. Sequencing rules: do not run two rebuilds of overlapping regions concurrently, and do not interleave with a full rebake — the build reads the asset's grid anchoring and the apply assumes it is unchanged since dispatch.

Swap rebuilt tiles (from [`RebuildTilesAsync`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshSurface~RebuildTilesAsync) or [`BuildTilesInBounds`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshBuilder~BuildTilesInBounds)) into the live TileCache and mirror them into the asset. Main thread only.

A cache with carve work in flight cannot take a swap, and draining it inline costs milliseconds per queued tile under the write lock — so the swap is held until the frame the pump reports the cache settled, usually the next one. Anything queuing tile work sets that flag, a link rebuild included. A cache that never settles (an obstacle moving every frame re-queues as fast as the pump drains) gives up after a few passes and pays the drain. Use [`ApplyRebuiltTilesImmediately`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshSurface~ApplyRebuiltTilesImmediately) when the tiles must be live before the call returns.

False only when there is nothing to apply to; true means applied OR held. A held swap keeps the layer blobs handed to it, so do not recycle them until it lands.

docs.remarks: Applies within the call instead of waiting for a settled frame: the swap quiesces pending obstacle work, replaces each tile's layers, refreshes every obstacle's touched-tile list (stale after a tile replacement bumps its salt), then rebuilds the new tiles with carves re-applied. Returns false, leaving the tiles as they were, when the cache cannot be quiesced. Called from a handler while a deferred swap is applying, it queues behind the swaps still waiting instead, since applying first would let them revert it.

docs.summary: Collect this surface's bake geometry from the scene (main thread), optionally restricted to objects whose bounds intersect `filterBounds`, a conservative test against transformed local bounds, so a partial rebuild's collection cost scales with the changed region. Volume mode composes: the volume intersects the filter.

Collect the scene's [`NavMeshModifierVolume`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshModifierVolume)s that apply to this surface's agent type (main thread), optionally restricted to volumes overlapping `filterBounds`. Same object scoping (CollectObjects/Layers) as geometry collection.

Collect the scene's [`NavMeshLink`](#api~Prowl.Runtime.NavMeshLink)s that apply to this surface's agent type (main thread), optionally restricted to links overlapping `filterBounds`. Same object scoping (CollectObjects/Layers) as geometry collection.
